$comment: Brand packs: one APK per brand, built from the SAME codebase and the SAME catalog.
A pack is not a fork. tools/apply_pack.py rewrites the package name and the app name
inside a fresh upstream checkout, and tools/gen_recipes.py --pack emits only that
pack's groups into Recipes.java. Everything else is byte-identical to the all-in-one app.
Two things make a pack work that are easy to miss:
1. The Android package name MUST differ per pack, or the packages cannot be installed
side by side (Android identifies an app by its package name; same name = an update).
2. The camera's settings store is shared between packs. Each pack keeps its own
snapshot (getFilesDir() is per-package), but only one recipe can be active on the
camera at a time. Installing three packs does NOT give you three cameras.
app_name is the string that lands in res/values/strings.xml. It is deliberately kept to
a <brand> + adjective form rather than a bare brand name or a camera model number:
naming a distributed app after a trademark implies endorsement, which is the risk that
actually gets a project taken down. See docs/BRAND-PACKS.md.
publish: false keeps a pack OUT of the release matrix (and out of build_apk.sh
--all-packs) without deleting it — it stays in the catalog, its tests still run, and it
can still be built one-off with tools/build_apk.sh <id> or looked up with
tools/build_matrix.py --apk-for <id>. Flip it back to true to ship it again.
Groups deliberately left out of every pack. They stay reachable in the all-in-one
app, which is still built and still published. Assigned here rather than silently
dropped, so the gap is visible in the data instead of in a bug report.
unassigned_groups.canon-nikon: spans two brands - needs one pack each before it can be split
unassigned_groups.pana-olympus: spans two brands - needs one pack each before it can be split
unassigned_groups.app-look: not a camera brand - social/app filter looks
